## The number that decides whether stage 5 is finished

It is not the overall rate. It is these two rows:

| | Wanted | On disk | |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Wall 1 packet** | 26 | 3 | 12% |
| **Identified designs** | 22 | 7 | 32% |

The Wall 1 packet holds the open ruling on whether this chapter has an identified core at all, and the identified designs carry whatever GRADE rating each arm gets. A rate computed over all 436 records answers neither question.

## The three worklists

Split by what would fix each record, because a blocked route and a paywall go to different people. On A.17, 67 of 98 failures were open urls killed by bot defence; handing all 98 to one person as "paywalled" would have wasted the 67 a browser opens in a second.

| Worklist | n | Of which critical | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `W1_browser` | 59 | 16 | a 200 that was not the article — open content behind bot defence, a splash page, or an abstract. A browser session opens these. |
| `W2_library_proxy` | 187 | 13 | no open location on any rung, but the record has a DOI. Genuinely closed; needs institutional access. |
| `W3_librarian` | 95 | 4 | no DOI at all. No proxy resolves these and no rung can construct a url — a catalogue search, an interlibrary request, or an author email. |

**33 of the 341 unretrieved records are critical** — Wall 1 packet or an identified design. They lead every worklist, because a worklist sorted by what is easy would put the 193 link-1 records first and leave the open ruling unread.

## What this does not claim

- **`W2` is closed by our evidence, not by the publisher's.** It means no rung this pipeline runs found an open copy. A copy on a personal page, in a repository OpenAlex does not index, or under a title variant is not ruled out.
- **`W1` is a prediction that a browser will work**, and it should be measured like any other rung — how many of the browser attempts actually delivered — rather than assumed.
